label: main season
summary: Recommend cancellation by non-technical survey for sign-off. Three distinct first-hand sources report 15–23 years of safe use/no finds or accidents; this exceeds the two-source, five-year criterion. The only contamination-related report is an unverified second-hand warning with no identifiable witness or location, explained by the sustained safe-use reports. No direct or higher-reliability indirect evidence is recorded, and the rule check passed. The nearest database accident is within 1 km, not inside this area.
flags: The zone survey flag and survey priority indicate where to visit, not evidence of contamination.

checks.detail: Every item of the evidence log is in the register.
There is no direct evidence and no indirect evidence of class 1 to 4, and every item of weaker indirect evidence is explained by evidence of absence of class 1 to 4.
3 different reliable source(s) report at least 5 years of safe use (E2; E3; E4); the criteria need 2.
No past landmine accident is recorded inside the area.

E1.quote: people should keep away from the area because of mines, but could not say who had seen anything, or where.
E1.note: This is an unverified second-hand warning with no identifiable first-hand source or location, so it suggests possible EO but is weak.

E2.quote: We have walked the trail across this land to the school for 16 years. Nobody has found anything, and nobody has been hurt.
E2.note: The teacher reports first-hand, long-term safe use across the area, supporting absence and accounting for the vague warning.

E3.quote: the board has recorded no find or accident in the area in the 15 years she has held the post, and that families use land in the area every week.
E3.note: The board president reports ongoing local use and no recorded finds or accidents over 15 years, supporting absence and accounting for the vague warning.

E4.quote: We have hunted and fished along these streams for 23 years. Nobody has found anything, and nobody has been hurt.
E4.note: The local hunter and fisher reports first-hand safe use of the area for 23 years, supporting absence and accounting for the vague warning.
